Keywords: @app.middleware http decorator add_process_time custom middleware async call_next
Description: The primary FastAPI way to add custom middleware — use the @app.middleware('http') decorator on an async function that receives Request and call_next. The docs show time.perf_counter() for process time headers.
Use Case: For adding custom request/response processing like timing headers or logging
Code Example:
"import time
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request

app = FastAPI()

@app.middleware('http')
async def add_process_time_header(request: Request, call_next):
    start_time = time.perf_counter()
    response = await call_next(request)
    process_time = time.perf_counter() - start_time
    response.headers['X-Process-Time'] = str(process_time)
    return response"
Configuration Tips: Custom proprietary headers should use the X- prefix. To expose custom headers to browsers also add them to CORS expose_headers.
Gotchas: Middleware runs for every request including static files and /docs — test it doesn't break Swagger UI

Keywords: cors CORSMiddleware cross origin allow_origins headers methods credentials starlette
Description: Enables cross-origin resource sharing. Required for any browser-based client on a different domain. Import from fastapi.middleware.cors. Set specific origins in production.
Use Case: Any API consumed by a frontend app on a different origin
Code Example:
"from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=['https://myapp.com'],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=['*'],
    allow_headers=['*'],
)"
Configuration Tips: In production use specific origins never wildcard ['*'] with allow_credentials=True — browsers block this combination.
Gotchas: Middleware order matters — add_middleware calls are applied in reverse order (last added = outermost). CORS should typically be added last so it is outermost.

Keywords: middleware order add_middleware stack execution reverse LIFO outermost
Description: FastAPI/Starlette applies middleware in reverse registration order — the last add_middleware call becomes the outermost wrapper. Request flows outer-to-inner; response flows inner-to-outer.
Use Case: Understanding or debugging middleware interaction order
Code Example:
"# Registered first = innermost (closest to route)
app.add_middleware(AuthMiddleware)
# Registered last = outermost (first to see requests)
app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware)

# Request order:  CORSMiddleware -> AuthMiddleware -> route
# Response order: route -> AuthMiddleware -> CORSMiddleware"
Configuration Tips: Document your middleware stack order explicitly — it's a common source of bugs when CORS preflight OPTIONS requests are rejected by auth middleware.
Gotchas: Always add CORSMiddleware last (outermost) so OPTIONS preflight requests are answered before auth runs

Keywords: gzip compress response large JSON file bandwidth starlette GZipMiddleware
Description: Compresses responses above a minimum size threshold using gzip. Reduces response payload size for bandwidth-constrained clients or large JSON responses.
Use Case: APIs returning large JSON payloads or file content
Configuration Tips: Set minimum_size to avoid compressing tiny responses where compression overhead exceeds savings. Default is 500 bytes.
Gotchas: Do not enable on endpoints that stream binary data — compression interferes with chunked streaming responses

Keywords: trusted host security Host header injection allowed_hosts starlette
Description: Rejects requests whose Host header does not match an allowed list. Prevents HTTP Host header injection attacks.
Use Case: Any production API exposed to the public internet
Configuration Tips: Include all valid hostnames including load balancer addresses. Use wildcards like '*.myapp.com' for subdomains.
Gotchas: Behind a reverse proxy the Host header may be rewritten by the proxy — verify the Host header seen by FastAPI

Keywords: BaseHTTPMiddleware class-based custom middleware starlette dispatch
Description: Starlette's BaseHTTPMiddleware is the class-based alternative to the @app.middleware decorator. Override dispatch() to implement custom logic.
Use Case: When you want reusable middleware classes that can be packaged or tested independently
Code Example:
"from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware
from fastapi import Request

class RequestIDMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    async def dispatch(self, request: Request, call_next):
        request.state.request_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        response = await call_next(request)
        response.headers['X-Request-ID'] = request.state.request_id
        return response

app.add_middleware(RequestIDMiddleware)"
Configuration Tips: BaseHTTPMiddleware buffers the full request body — for streaming you must use @app.middleware decorator or pure ASGI middleware.
Gotchas: BaseHTTPMiddleware has known compatibility issues with some streaming response types — prefer @app.middleware for simple use cases

Keywords: https redirect ssl tls secure force production HTTP starlette
Description: Redirects any plain HTTP request to HTTPS. Use in production deployments where TLS is terminated by FastAPI itself. Skip if your proxy (nginx Caddy) already handles redirects.
Use Case: APIs deployed without a TLS-terminating proxy that need to enforce HTTPS
Configuration Tips: Only enable in production. Disable during local development. Verify your proxy is not already redirecting to avoid double-redirect loops.
Gotchas: If you are behind an nginx or Caddy proxy with TLS your proxy handles this already — adding this middleware causes double redirects

Keywords: session cookie browser server-side SessionMiddleware secret_key signed
Description: Provides signed cookie-based sessions. The session dict is stored in a cookie — not server-side. Use for lightweight browser state.
Use Case: Web UIs served by FastAPI needing lightweight per-user state (flash messages selected language)
Configuration Tips: Generate secret_key with: python -c \import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))\" — never hardcode."
Gotchas: Session data is in the cookie (not server-side). Cookie is limited to ~4 KB. Never store sensitive data (tokens passwords) in session cookies.
